newsitem.title: GERMANY: Growth in German TV ad market seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Growth in German TV ad market seen slowing.

text.p: Growth in Germany's TV advertising market is becoming less dynamic and the years of double-digit expansion have become a thing of the past, the country's central advertising association (ZAW) said on Wednesday.

ZAW spokesman Volker Nickel said that, according to a study by advertising sellers IP Deutschland, overall TV ad revenues would grow this year by around five percent to between 7.2 and 7.3 billion marks ($4.4 billion).
In future, Nickel added, sellers of advertising time will be competing increasingly for market share rather than cashing in on a growing overall ad budget.
The IP Deutschland study predicts annual growth rates in TV advertising revenues of between five and six percent in the years up to 2000, IP spokesman Andreas Kuehner said.
Germany, which has 18 commercial TV stations, is an "oversaturated" market. That will result in competition which could force small broadcasters out of business, Kuehner said.
Last year, TV advertising revenues were around seven billion marks. Newspapers pulled in revenues of 11 billion marks, while other print media earned 3.5 billion marks.
Nickel added that overall advertising market growth would be between two and three percent annually over the next three years.
The ZAW will present its final advertising figures for 1996 in May. ($ = 1.653 German Marks)
